title: 36 · conch · The Conch
lines: n
In a Shiva temple, you never pour water from a conch.
n
Every other god loves it. Here is why he does not.
n
There was a demon king named Shankhachuda. The conch-crowned.
n
He was not cruel. He was unbeatable.
Protected by a boon, and by a wife whose faith never wavered.
n
But he drove the gods out of heaven.
And the gods went to Shiva.
n
Shiva fought him for a hundred years.
His trident could not land.
n
Then the protection was taken away.
Not by strength. By a trick of Vishnu's that Shiva never liked.
n
The trident fell.
n
Shankhachuda's bones dropped into the ocean,
and became every conch shell in the sea.
n
Vishnu holds a conch in every picture. He honours it.
n
But Shiva remembers the king it once was.
He will not be bathed with the bones of one he had to kill.
n
So you offer him water from your hands.
Know the story behind the rule. That is sadhana.
n
